title: Mechanism Mapping
description: DISCOVER-stage downstream artifact (Explicit analogy mapping cluster). Output of analogy-mapper. Takes an EXISTING transfer_candidates item (a cross-domain candidate already surfaced by cross-domain-transfer-scout) plus a problem_abstraction, and turns the informal 'is this retrieved cross-domain paper a real structural analog' judgment into a TYPED, scored, checkable artifact: it lays the source-domain mechanisms next to the target-problem mechanisms, records which mechanisms are SHARED, which source assumptions would BLOCK the transfer, and which ADAPTATIONS are required. overlap_score is computed (set by tools/analogy_graph_match.match_mechanisms, never hand-set). The verdict is PASS / REPAIR / REJECT. The allOf below mirrors the derivation-verdict family in this repo (sanity_verdict / venue_readiness_verdict): a 'PASS' verdict structurally REQUIRES blocking_assumptions to be empty (maxItems 0) — so a 'PASS with unresolved blockers' is impossible to even write. analogy-mapper consumes transfer_candidates; it does NOT redefine it, fetch papers, or decide final selection. Domain-general: no domain is hardcoded (medical-imaging / NLP / RL are just instances of source_domain).

mapping_id.description: Short unique identifier for this mapping, e.g. AM-001. Non-blank required.

source_domain.description: The domain the analogous mechanism originates from (carried from the transfer_candidates item's source_domain), e.g. 'natural language processing', 'graph neural networks'. Non-blank required.

target_problem_id.description: Identifier of the target-problem / problem_abstraction this mapping is scored against (e.g. a target_hook id or a problem_abstraction id). Non-blank required.

shared_mechanisms.description: The mechanisms that genuinely appear in BOTH the source domain and the target problem — the structural core of the analogy. At least one required (a mapping with zero shared mechanisms is not an analogy and must not be emitted as one).

mechanism.description: A mechanism-level phrase shared by source and target (domain nouns stripped), e.g. 'propagate labels along a sparse graph', 'segment thin elongated structure'. Non-blank required.

source_evidence_ref.description: Anti-slop: at least one non-blank pointer (the transfer_candidates evidence_ref / a real source-domain paper ref) grounding that this mechanism is real in the source domain.

target_hook.description: Optional: where in the target problem this shared mechanism applies (carried from the transfer_candidates item's target_hook).

blocking_assumptions.description: Source-domain assumptions that would BREAK the transfer if they do not hold in the target problem. EMPTY iff the analogy carries no unresolved blocker. A non-empty list forbids a PASS verdict (see allOf).

assumption.description: The source-domain assumption at risk in the target problem, e.g. 'source method assumes dense supervision'. Non-blank required.

why_blocking.description: Why this assumption blocks the transfer in the target problem. Non-blank required.

evidence_ref.description: Optional pointers grounding the blocking assumption.

required_adaptations.description: Concrete changes needed to make the source mechanism work on the target problem (the 'how to port it' list). May be empty when the transfer is direct.

adaptation.description: The concrete adaptation, e.g. 'replace dense loss with a sparse-label variant'. Non-blank required.

addresses.description: Which blocking_assumption.assumption or shared mechanism this adaptation addresses. Non-blank required.

overlap_score.description: Mechanism-set overlap in [0,1], COMPUTED by tools/analogy_graph_match.match_mechanisms (Jaccard of the source vs target mechanism sets) — never hand-set. A score alone never decides the verdict (it informs it).

verdict.description: PASS: a real structural analog with NO unresolved blocking assumptions (allOf forbids PASS while blocking_assumptions is non-empty). REPAIR: a plausible analog but blocked until the required_adaptations are made / blocking_assumptions resolved. REJECT: not a real structural analog (mechanisms do not actually overlap).

notes.description: Optional free-text caveats, north-star drift notes, or why a borderline analog got its verdict.
